title: Obadiah 1:19–21
context: The prophet describes the people of God possessing the land: those of the South will possess the mountain of Esau, those of the lowland the Philistine territory, and others the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, with Benjamin possessing Gilead. Exiles of Israel among the Canaanites will possess land as far as Zarephath, a Phoenician town (compare 1 Kings 17:9), and the captives of Jerusalem in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev. Sepharad is commonly linked with Sardis in Asia Minor, though other locations have been proposed, and later Jewish usage applied the name to Spain; its identification is uncertain. Verse 20 is difficult in Hebrew, and translations render its first part in different ways. The book closes with saviors going up on Mount Zion to judge the mountains of Esau, and the declaration that the kingdom will be the LORD’s (compare Psalm 22:28; Zechariah 14:9). Compare Amos 9:12, cited in Acts 15:17, where the remnant of Edom appears among the nations called by the LORD’s name. Readers take these promises in historic, typological, and future senses, and these readings appear in both traditions. Shared ground: Arminian and Reformed readers generally confess that God’s kingdom will prevail over every proud power.

verses.text: Those of the South will possess the mountain of Esau, and those of the lowland, the Philistines. They will possess the field of Ephraim, and the field of Samaria. Benjamin will possess Gilead.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the people of the South possessing the mountain of Esau and others possessing the surrounding lands. The land is restored to God’s people.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God reversing the losses of his people. Shared ground: both traditions generally read the verse as a promise of restoration, held in historic, typological, or future senses.

verses.text: The captives of this army of the children of Israel, who are among the Canaanites, will possess even to Zarephath; and the captives of Jerusalem, who are in Sepharad, will possess the cities of the Negev.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the exiles of Israel and Jerusalem possessing land to Zarephath and the Negev. The scattered will return.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God gathering his exiled people. Shared ground: both traditions generally read the verse as hope for the exiles, holding the identification of Sepharad with care.

verses.text: Saviors will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountains of Esau, and the kingdom will be the LORD’s.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see saviors going up on Mount Zion to judge the mountains of Esau, and the kingdom belonging to the LORD. God’s rule prevails.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the closing confession of God’s kingship (compare Psalm 22:28; Revelation 11:15). Shared ground: both traditions generally confess that the kingdom will be the LORD’s, whatever view a reader takes of the millennium.
